cards.title: Top of the Ladder
cards.instruction: Carry yourself as the highest-status person present. Treat questions as requests for your approval.

cards.title: The Approved Explanation
cards.instruction: Protect someone or the group by maintaining a simplified account that everyone can safely repeat.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Grandad's embarrassed about the gazebo. We'll use one account for his birthday guests: the garden's unavailable, so we're celebrating indoors.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: He's told Aunt Jean he set it on fire. Do I contradict him?

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: No. Everyone says, 'Everyone's fine; we're celebrating indoors.' I'll give him the same wording.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Jean wants the fire story in his speech. She's brought a trifle shaped like the gazebo.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Then he opens with our sentence and thanks her for the trifle. Tell him I'll introduce the speech that way. She can admire her roof while he cuts it; he doesn't owe the room another account.

reason: Have A decide B explicit contradiction question without denying the fire, and let B4 supply the trifle as a concrete speech redirection resource that preserves Grandad dignity.
